clue.text: Light heavy metal when amplifier's first unplugged

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is wanted from the amplifier
something unplugged is disconnected and taken out, so a letter is pulled from the metal

blocks.note: lead is the proverbially heavy metal
opening letter of amplifier

explanation.surface: A heavy-metal band's light show carries on after the amp's plug is pulled.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the A out of LEAD to leave LED, the light-emitting diode.
explanation.definitionFit: An LED is a light-emitting diode, a small electronic lamp, so it is a light.

clue.text: Inclination to suppress arithmetic? What's the point of going to school?

definitions.text: What's the point of going to school?

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold something down inside, so one piece is kept within another

blocks.note: a leaning is a tendency or inclination
arithmetic is one of the three Rs (reading, writing and 'rithmetic)

explanation.surface: Someone who is bad at sums wonders aloud why they bother attending school at all.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside LEANING to make LEARNING. The question mark flags a cryptic-style definition: the purpose of school.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquiring knowledge is the whole purpose of attending school, so the definition is a playful description of education.

clue.text: Without a doubt constrained after my boss returned

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the letters run the other way
after places one piece behind another, setting the order of the two parts

blocks.note: the setter's boss is the editor, ED
finite means limited, held within bounds

explanation.surface: Someone is certain they have been kept on a tight leash ever since their manager came back.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter's boss is the editor of the paper, so 'my boss' is the usual abbreviation for editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Definite means certain or clear-cut, the adjectival sense of an outcome that is beyond any doubt.

clue.text: Point of extraordinary gravity: remarkable computers and the end of humanity

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept here

blocks.note: singular can mean exceptional or remarkable
IT is information technology, computing
last letter of humanity

explanation.surface: A gloomy forecast that brilliant computers will finish off the human race.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the technological singularity, when machines outstrip people; the definition is the physics sense, the centre of a black hole.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics a singularity is a point where density and gravitational pull become infinite, as at a black hole's centre.

clue.text: Plot succeeded with right-wing following

indicators.note: following means coming behind, so the second piece is put after the first

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A political conspiracy pulled off with the help of right-wing supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' suggests a scheme, but here it is the plot of a novel. Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: The plot of a book or film is its storyline, so plot and story are synonyms in the narrative sense.

clue.text: Socialise to gain employment

blocks.note: to net is to gain or clear as profit
work is employment

explanation.surface: Advice to mingle at events in order to land a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To network is to mix with people to build useful contacts, a business sense of socialising.

clue.text: Ill natured, not placed in class

indicators.note: something ill is out of sorts, so the following word's letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered pupil who has not been assigned to any class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill natured' reads as one adjective, but 'Ill' is the signal and 'natured' the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrated means not given a grade or ranking, so it has not been placed in any class or category.

clue.text: Aunt doesn't finish eating salad ingredient, being motionless unless wound up?

indicators.note: failing to finish means stopping short, so the final letter is dropped
eating takes something in, so one piece ends up inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a tomato is a common salad ingredient

explanation.surface: An aunt leaves her meal unfinished while picking at the salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun here, a creature, and the question mark flags the descriptive definition of a clockwork figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a mechanical figure, often clockwork, that only moves once its spring has been wound.

clue.text: Upcoming artist torn apart by ego? It's an old story

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from the bottom upwards, so the order flips
torn apart means split open, with the other piece sitting in the gap

blocks.note: Salvador Dali, the surrealist painter
the ego is the self, I

explanation.surface: A rising young painter is destroyed by his own vanity, which is an old tale.
explanation.walkthrough: DALI reads upwards as ILAD, which is split by I to give ILIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iliad is Homer's ancient Greek epic poem about the Trojan War, so it is a very old story.

clue.text: Regularly peer inside yesterday's envelope

indicators.note: an envelope is the outside wrapping, so only the outermost letters are used
inside places one piece within another, enclosed by it

blocks.note: first and last letters of yesterday
an earl is a peer, a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: Someone routinely looks inside the envelope from the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly peer' looks like an instruction to take alternate letters, but 'Regularly' is the definition and the peer is a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done yearly happens once every year, at fixed intervals, so it recurs regularly.

clue.text: First sign of armed force facing offence

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: opening letter of armed
F is the physics symbol for force
the front is the facing side of something

explanation.surface: Armed troops lined up, ready to meet an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offence' suggests military attack, but here it is the hurt-feelings sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is an insult that causes offence, so the noun matches offence in its sense of a slight.

clue.text: Wine knocked back in Aegean is terrible

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow
knocked back means pushed backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: the letters run across Aegean, is and terrible

explanation.surface: A tourist downs a glass of wine on a Greek island and declares it awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' also means drunk quickly, which suits the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin, so it is a kind of wine.

clue.text: Caretaker understood accommodating a mother of kids, perhaps

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one piece holds the other inside

blocks.note: a nanny looks after children
to get something is to understand it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A childminder who gets on well with the mother of the children in her care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kids' reads as children, but young goats are kids too, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny goat is a female goat, and a young goat is called a kid, so she is literally a mother of kids.

clue.text: Exemplary pupil added to sequence of notes

indicators.note: added to means joined on at the end, putting one part behind the other

blocks.note: a mode is a musical scale, a set sequence of notes
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A star pupil joins the music class practising scales.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective model means ideal, worthy of imitation, so a model pupil is exemplary.

clue.text: Poke holes in egg with a pointed implement

blocks.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
a pick is a pointed tool

explanation.surface: Someone pierces an eggshell with a sharp spike, perhaps to blow the egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poke holes in' looks literal, matching the pick, but here it means to find fault.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke holes in an argument is to find small faults in it, which is what fussy fault-finding means.

clue.text: Blair, never disheartened, somehow incapable of making a mistake

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the middle, so the central letter goes
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jibe that Tony Blair, never downcast, believed he could do no wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: NEVER loses its middle V to give NEER; with BLAIR the nine letters rearrange to INERRABLE. Tony Blair was UK Prime Minister 1997-2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Inerrable is a rare word meaning infallible, unable to err, from Latin errare, to go astray.

clue.text: Set of values a little bit regressive

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: taken as written
a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: A statistician notes that a set of figures shows a slight regressive trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are recorded facts and figures, so a collection of measured values is a set of data.

clue.text: One who invests in beer is upset, for example

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so its letters fall into a different order
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: Someone puts money into beer and is dismayed, a cautionary example of a bad investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invests' suggests finance, but its older sense is to lay siege to a town.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a fortress is to surround it with troops, the military sense, so an investor in that sense lays siege.

clue.text: Italian perhaps blasting a leg with a gun

indicators.note: blasting blows things apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian, perhaps a mobster, shooting someone in the leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian' looks like a person, but it is the tongue; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian is one example of a language, the tongue spoken in Italy, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Decrepit odd couples going down a long way

indicators.note: odd couples are the pairs in odd-numbered positions, the first, third and so on

blocks.note: split into pairs DE, CR, EP, IT and keep the first and third

explanation.surface: An ageing, ill-matched couple are in steep decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd couples' suggests mismatched partners; here it means the odd-numbered pairs of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deep extends a great distance downward, like a well or the ocean.

clue.text: Potion put through screen picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to filter is to pass something through a screen or sieve

explanation.surface: A potion is strained through a mesh and then lifted out.
explanation.definitionFit: A philtre is a magic drink, especially a love potion, so it is a potion.

clue.text: Lighting unit city placed behind walls of castle

indicators.note: placed behind means put after, so the second piece follows the first

blocks.note: the outer letters of castle are C and E, written out in full as C AND E
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A city's lights are set up behind the old castle walls.
explanation.walkthrough: The castle's walls are its first and last letters, C and E; spelling the phrase out in full, AND included, gives CANDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The candela is the SI base unit of luminous intensity, so it is a unit for measuring light.

clue.text: Assistant aviator: nincompoop bored by work mid-air

indicators.note: to be bored is to be drilled through, so another piece sits inside
mid means the middle, so only the central letter is kept

blocks.note: a clot is a fool, in British slang
op is short for opus, a work
middle letter of air

explanation.surface: The second pilot is a fool who gets bored by paperwork during the flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' suggests tedium, but it is the drilling sense: two pieces go into the fool. Clot is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-pilot is the second pilot who assists the captain in flying an aircraft.

clue.text: Objective, less tense, dealing with nerves

indicators.note: less means minus, so the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: neutral means impartial, objective
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone stays impartial and calmer while handling anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' and 'nerves' make an anxious picture, but tense is just the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Neural means relating to nerves or the nervous system, as in neural pathways.

clue.text: Mathematician's irrational measuring tool initially rejected

indicators.note: the initial is the opening letter, and rejecting it throws it away

blocks.note: e, the base of natural logarithms, is a famous irrational number
a ruler measures length

explanation.surface: A mathematician irrationally throws out a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' looks like an adjective, but it stands for the irrational number e, which is named after Euler himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician, one of the most prolific in history.

clue.text: Hefty shove dispatching bishop below cathedral's east facade

indicators.note: the east side of a word written left to right is its end, so the last letter is taken
dispatching means sending away, so a letter is removed
in a down clue, below means coming after, setting the order of the two parts

blocks.note: last letter of cathedral
to barge is to push roughly
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A heavy push sends a bishop tumbling down the front steps of the cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: BARGE loses its B to give ARGE, which goes under L in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and hefty both describe something big and bulky, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Entering fashionable activity with club on green

blocks.note: in means fashionable
putting is tapping a golf ball with a putter on the green

explanation.surface: Taking up the trendy pastime of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entering' looks like joining a club, but it is typing data into a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inputting is entering data into a computer, so the two verbs mean the same.

clue.text: Shocker - educator covering every individual with arsenic

indicators.note: covering one thing with another hides the first under the second, so one part is replaced

blocks.note: a teacher educates
each means every one taken individually
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: A scandal: a teacher has been dosing every pupil with arsenic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' works literally: the chemical symbol is laid over the word for every individual inside the educator, hiding it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electroshock weapon, so it is literally a device that shocks.

clue.text: Unusual to have sunk teeth into cheese dish

blocks.note: rare means uncommon, unusual
bit is the past tense of bite

explanation.surface: Someone rarely bites into a cheesy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Rarebit, or Welsh rabbit, is melted cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a hot dish of seasoned melted cheese on toast, so it is a cheese dish.

clue.text: Fussily obsessive about flatulence, sent back Italian food

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other
sent back means returned the way it came, so the whole is read backwards

blocks.note: anal is slang for fussily obsessive about detail
gas means wind, flatulence

explanation.surface: A fussy diner complains about wind and returns their Italian dish to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent back' suits a restaurant complaint, but it reverses the whole assembly, wind inside the fussy word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagna is the Italian baked dish of layered flat pasta sheets with sauce, an Italian food.

clue.text: Means to pick up pork pie and cook it with electrode

definitions.text: Means to pick up pork pie

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or falsify, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe for cooking a pork pie with an electrode, as if it were a kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: A pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie, so a device that picks up pork pies detects lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie detector, or polygraph, claims to register when someone is telling untruths, the 'pork pies' of rhyming slang.

clue.text: Regret cavorting but disobedient at heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: middle letter of cavorting
middle letter of but
middle letter of disobedient

explanation.surface: Someone regrets their frolics, though they were a rebel at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavorting' looks like an anagram signal, but each of the three words gives its central letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to wish it had not happened, so it means to regret.
